newsitem.title: UK: KPMG says 1996 revenues up 8 pct to $8.1 bln.
newsitem.headline: KPMG says 1996 revenues up 8 pct to $8.1 bln.

text.p: International accounting and consulting group KPMG said on Tuesday that its worldwide revenues for the 1996 fiscal year, ending September 30, grew by eight percent to $8.1 billion.
"The total represents overall growth of 8.0 percent, when compared with the firm's 1995 revenues of $7.5 billion," KPMG said in a statement.

KPMG said the growth had come in a year when it had made "significant investment in developing and implementing new products and services, as well as upgrading the firm's technology around the globe".
The firm said these investments were part of KPMG's strategy to grow the consulting part of its business more quickly.
"Our priority this past year was to make major investments in new products and services to enhance future growth," KPMG International chairman Jon Madonna said.
"We need to grow faster and will do so through these new products and services," he added.

During the year, KPMG launched a "comprehensive financial and strategic analysis for clients that provides value-added information beyond the traditional audit". It also unveiled "Global Tax Vision" which focuses on strategic tax planning.
